neighbours.label: reassuring promise to the reader in advice or sales prose ('surely you will', 'you will be given')
fire: Follow these five steps every morning and surely you will notice a difference within a week.
Keep revising the old papers and you will definitely pass the board exam this year.
Sign up to our newsletter today and you will be given a free shipping voucher.
Stick with the plan for a month and surely your skin will look brighter.
Read one chapter a night and you will certainly finish the series before summer.
Water the seedlings twice a day and surely they will sprout by next weekend.
Join the loyalty club now and you will be rewarded with points on every purchase.
Practise the scales slowly and you will surely play the piece without mistakes.
quiet: Follow the river path for five miles and the trail ends at an old mill.
She revised the old papers on the train and handed them in on Monday.
The newsletter goes out every Friday and lists the week's new arrivals.
He stuck to the plan for a month and then moved to another city.
The library opens at nine and the reading room closes at six.
The seedlings were planted in March and moved outside in May.
The loyalty club was launched in 2015 by a small group of shop owners.
The pianist practised the scales slowly before the evening concert began.
